CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS owners (
  id INTEGER GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  title VARCHAR(10),
  first_name VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
  last_name VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
  address VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  address_line1 VARCHAR(255),
  address_line2 VARCHAR(255),
  city VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
  postcode VARCHAR(4),
  telephone VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  email VARCHAR(255),
  registration_date DATE,
  birth_date DATE,
  customer_code VARCHAR(20),
  household_id VARCHAR(64),
  namesake_count INTEGER,
  household_size INTEGER,
  bulk_signup_warning BOOLEAN,
  possible_duplicate BOOLEAN,
  possible_duplicate_of INTEGER,
  deleted BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE

All 10 tests pass (`BUILD SUCCESS`). Here's what I implemented and why.

## The rule
A new owner's `membershipLevel` is capped at one above the highest membership level among existing members of the same household; with no existing household member, no cap applies.

## Changes

**New pipeline step — `CapMembershipLevel`** (`rest/function/owner/`): scans existing owners sharing the new owner's household id (reusing `HouseholdNormalizer.belongsTo`), takes the max of their `MembershipLevel.forPoints(MembershipPoints.of(...))`, and stores `max + 1` as the ceiling — or `null` when there is no household member. Modeled on the sibling `CountHousehold`/`CountNamesakes` steps; single responsibility.

**`Owner`** — added a persisted `membershipLevelCap` (`membership_level_cap` column, added to all four DB schemas: hsqldb/h2/postgres/mysql, since tests run `ddl-auto=none`). The cap is a creation-time snapshot, mirroring how `householdSize`/`namesakeCount` are stored.

**`OwnerMapper.membershipLevel`** — still derives the banded level from points, then holds it down to the stored ceiling (`Math.min(level, cap)` when a cap is present). The derivation stays in `MembershipLevel`; the mapper just wires the derived value to the stored cap.

**`owners.POST.yml`** — inserted `capMembershipLevel` (under `transaction` governance) right after `countHousehold`, before `save`.

## One necessary supporting fix
The new test creates two distinct owners in the *same* household, which `EnsureUniqueIdentity` was rejecting as a 409 on household-id alone — making the cap unobservable. But `FlagPossibleDuplicate`'s own contract already documents that a household member *"giving a different telephone... is allowed but marked for follow-up"* — meaning that branch was unreachable dead code. I aligned `EnsureUniqueIdentity` with that documented design: a hard duplicate is now same household **and** same telephone; distinct household members pass the block (then get flagged and capped). Updated the javadoc on both `EnsureUniqueIdentity` and `DuplicateIdentityException` to match.
